title: Genshiken
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Shy freshman Kanji Sasahara joins Genshiken, a university club for otaku, and over four years learns to accept his hobbies without shame. Alongside him are Saki Kasukabe, a non-otaku trying to drag her boyfriend out of the club, and Chika Ogiue, a fan who hates her own interests.
life_message: It holds up accepting oneself and one's passions, and friendship among misfits, as the way to grow up.

content.note: Buying and making erotic doujinshi and discussing eroge are recurring plot points; anime nudity was censored on TV (Wikipedia); AniList Boys' Love 20%.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Teasing and disputes are absorbed into club friendship (Wikipedia plot).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Members follow their hobbies freely, against social stigma (Wikipedia premise).

Civic vs kin.evidence: The club, not family, is the community (Wikipedia plot).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Club presidents and senpai exist but the room is informal (Wikipedia plot).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-acceptance of identity and hobbies is the arc (Wikipedia: Sasahara 'comes to accept himself').

folkways.japan: Social stigma around being otaku, senpai-kohai ties in the club and Comic Market culture reflect early-2000s Japanese fandom; IGN called it the definitive portrait of anime fandom.

delivery.evidence: Self-acceptance of otaku carried by club life and character arcs; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: Shame and conformity are gently challenged through the members' growth, per summaries.

winners_losers: The otaku and those who learn to accept them win sympathy; shame and conformity are gently challenged.
